name: Codewhale
description: Open-source agent for the terminal written in Rust. Use any provider or model. Issues & PRs always welcome
readmeExcerpt:
**An open-source coding agent for your terminal that works with any model.** Give Codewhale a task and it reads the repository, edits files, and runs commands until the task is done or it needs input from you. It works with more than 40 built-in providers, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash by default, and with models running on your own machine. `/receipts` lists the files it changed, the commands it ran, and the web and MCP calls it made. [Website](https://codewhale.net) · [Documentation](docs/README.md) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) [简体中文](docs/i18n/README.zh-CN.md) · [日本語](docs/i18n/README.ja-JP.md) · [Tiếng Việt](docs/i18n/README.vi.md) · [Bahasa Indonesia](docs/i18n/README.id.md) · [한국어](docs/i18n/README.ko-KR.md) · [Español](docs/i18n/README.es-419.md) · [Português](docs/i18n/README.pt-BR.md) · [Русский](docs/i18n/README.ru.md) · [Українська](docs/i18n/README.uk.md) · [Français](docs/i18n/README.fr.md) · [Deutsch](docs/i18n/README.de.md) · [繁體中文](docs/i18n/README.zh-TW.md) · [हिन्दी](docs/i18n/README.hi.md) · [Türkçe](docs/i18n/README.tr.md) · [Italiano](docs/i18n/README.it.md) · [Polski](docs/i18n/README.pl.md) · [العربية](docs/i18n/README.ar.md) · [Català](docs/i18n/README.ca.md) A 0.10.2 development build with a scripted test model, in Full Access inside a throwaway workspace. The edit, three tests and a sub-agent review ran for real.

[View the Codewhale × OrcaRouter offer](https://www.orcarouter.ai/redeem/1a6250545fdc4e0aaccb0a4470159e67). Codewhale earns a referral fee from OrcaRouter. ## Install macOS and Linux: ```bash curl -fsSL https://codewhale.net/install.sh | sh ``` The installer puts checksum-verified `codewhale` and its short alias `codew` in `~/.local/bin`. If your shell then says `command not found`, run the PATH line the installer prints ([details](docs/INSTALL.md#put-it-on-your-path)). `codewhale update` upgrades it. These commands install the latest release. This page follows `main`, so a feature marked with a version arrives in that release; the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md) lists what each release adds.
Windows, npm, Cargo, and other ways to install ```bash winget install HunterBown.CodeWhale # Windows x64 (or Scoop, or the installer from GitHub Releases) npm install -g codewhale # wraps the same release binaries cargo install codewhale-cli --locked # crates.io; can trail GitHub Releases ``` Prebuilt binaries cover Linux, macOS, and Windows on x64 and arm64. Nix, Homebrew on Linux, Android/Termux (preview), and manual downloads are in the [installation guide](docs/INSTALL.md), and containers in [Docker](docs/DOCKER.md). Stick to one install method per machine; otherwise two copies end up on `PATH` and whichever comes first wins.
## Quickstart 1. Commit or stash your work, then run `codewhale` from the root of a git repository. By default (**Accept Edits**) it edits files in the repository without asking and asks before each command; `Shift+Tab` steps the permission dial when you want it to ask more or less. 2. Run `/provider` (or press `F3`), pick a provider, paste its API key, and choose a model. DeepSeek is the default provider. With no key, pick a local runtime instead. If no provider is configured and Ollama is already serving a chat model, Codewhale uses it automatically; from 0.10.2 it offers it when you send your first message. 3. Type a task: ```text Fix the failing tests and explain what changed. ``` Read-only commands run straight away. For any other shell command Codewhale asks first: `y` runs it once, `a` allows commands like it for the rest of the conversation, `n` refuses. `/undo` takes back your last request and its file changes. `/help` lists commands and keys. For scripts and CI, `codewhale exec` runs one task without the interface. By default, `--auto` uses Full Access: tools run without asking, shell commands have no Codewhale sandbox, and trust mode lets file tools write outside the workspace. Add `--sandbox workspace-write` to keep the shell sandbox and file-tool workspace restrictions, with trust mode off: ```bash codewhale exec --auto --sandbox workspace-write "fix the failing tests and explain what changed" ``` ## Modes and permissions A fresh install starts in Work mode with the Accept Edits permission. One dial switches both: `Shift+Tab` steps Ask → Accept Edits → Plan → Auto-Review → Full Access. | | Switch with | Options | | --- | --- | --- | | Mode | the Plan stop on `Shift+Tab`, or `/mode` | **Plan** reads and searches but changes nothing. **Work** (every other stop) edits files and runs commands; start a goal with `/goal` when a request needs more than one turn. | | Permission | `Shift+Tab` | **Ask** asks before every file edit and every shell command that is not read-only. **Accept Edits** applies file edits in your git repository without asking and still asks before commands. **Auto-Review** lets rules and a reviewer model approve routine calls and refuses high-risk ones; switch to Ask to approve those yourself. **Full Access** never asks, and commands can reach anything on this computer; repository rules and managed policy still apply. | See the [modes and permissions guide](docs/MODES.md) for the details. ## What it does ### New in 0.10.2 - `/pet on` turns your terminal into an animated whale that shows what the agent is doing, while the message box stays live. Its 980 particles spell the current step in English, Chinese or Japanese. - `/workbar terminal` shows the shells the agent is running as they run. Type into one, or press `Ctrl+N` for a shell of your own (macOS and Linux). - `/undo` takes back your whole last request in one step, including every file it changed, and `/diff` works in folders without Git. - When a plan is ready, Codewhale asks whether to start Work with Ask or Auto-Review, or keep planning. - `/color` gives each chat its own composer color, saved with the session. - `web_search` can use DeepSeek's new Search API: set `[search] provider = "deepseek"` with a DeepSeek key. - Outside Full Access, a `curl` or `wget` that would upload a credential never runs without your approval, and a command that hides invisible Unicode is refused. `write` no longer replaces a file the agent has not read, or one that changed after it read it. ### Models More than 40 providers are built in, including Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Google, Mistral, Moonshot, OpenRouter, and xAI. Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works, and so do local models through Ollama, vLLM, or SGLang. The default is DeepSeek's `deepseek-flash`, which DeepSeek moved to DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 on 2026-10-17; 0.10.1 runs it without an update ([details](docs/PROVIDERS.md#deepseek-v41-flash)). `/model` switches models between turns, and `/model auto` picks one for each turn (`/router` sets up how). `/turn inspect` shows which model a turn used, what it cost and how long it took. `codewhale auth chatgpt` lets you use a ChatGPT plan instead of an API key (experimental). See [Providers](docs/PROVIDERS.md). ### Receipts and undo `/receipts`, or `codewhale receipts --last` after you quit, lists the files changed, commands run, web and MCP calls, agents started, approvals and who gave them, and failures. `/undo` takes back your last request and the files it changed, in one step and without trust mode. `/restore` rolls the whole workspace back to an earlier snapshot; because that overwrites later edits, it needs `/trust on` or Full Access. See [Receipts](docs/RECEIPTS.md). Exec runs that offer tools are saved in every output format, so `codewhale receipts --last` works after `exec --auto`, including `--json`. Answer-only text and `--json` runs are saved only when resuming or when conversation compaction starts; use `--output-format stream-json` to always save them for receipts or `exec --continue`. ### Longer work `/goal` sets an objective that carries across turns. Codewhale can split work across [sub-agents](docs/SUBAGENTS.md), run a [fleet](docs/FLEET.md) of agents, or follow a [workflow](docs/WORKFLOW_AUTHORING.md) checked into the repository. ### Coming from another agent Codewhale reads `AGENTS.md` on its own. Instruction files written for other tools, such as `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursorrules`, or `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, load only when you opt in with `project_instruction_imports = ["claude"]` (or `"cursor"`, `"cline"`, `"windsurf"`, `"copilot"`, `"all"`) in your config; see [config.example.toml](config.example.toml). Codewhale warns when it finds one it did not load. `/import-claude` prepares an import of your Claude Code settings and MCP servers for you to review. `/plugin install` accepts Claude Code plugins containing skills, commands, agent profiles, and MCP servers, and refuses plugins that need hooks or LSP servers ([details](docs/CLAUDE_PLUGIN_COMPAT.md)). ### Extensions Connect [MCP servers](docs/MCP.md), add [skills](docs/SKILLS.md) and [plugins](docs/PLUGINS.md), and run [hooks](docs/HOOKS.md) on session and tool events. Code mode (experimental, on by default) lets the model write one `execute_tools` program that calls several MCP and plugin tools; each call still meets your approval rules and keeps its receipt. The independently installed Computer Use plugin (experimental, macOS only) can observe and operate other apps. It stays off until you review its access and enable it ([guide](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/codewhale-cu-plugin)). ## Ways to run it | Command | What it does | | --- | --- | | `codewhale` | The interactive terminal app | | `codewhale exec "…"` | One task without the interface. On its own it answers without using tools; `--auto` enables tools with Full Access by default, `--sandbox workspace-write` restricts them, and `--output-format stream-json` streams events as JSON | | `codewhale web` | A local web UI on `127.0.0.1` ([guide](docs/WEB.md)) | | `codewhale review --pr N` | An advisory review of a GitHub pull request. The [GitHub bot setup](docs/GITHUB_ACTION.md#set-up-your-own-bot) generates a pinned workflow for automatic reviews and `@codewhale review`, using your own model key and optional App identity | | `codewhale app-server --http` | The [Runtime API](docs/RUNTIME_API.md), a local HTTP API for threads, events, approvals, and each turn's file changes | | `codewhale serve --acp` | The Agent Client Protocol over stdio, for editors such as Zed | The terminal app, `exec`, `web`, and the Runtime API share one engine ([architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)). readmeHtml:
An open-source coding agent for your terminal that works with any model.

Give Codewhale a task and it reads the repository, edits files, and runs commands until the task is done or it needs input from you. It works with more than 40 built-in providers, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash by default, and with models running on your own machine. /receipts lists the files it changed, the commands it ran, and the web and MCP calls it made.

Website · Documentation · Changelog · Contributing

简体中文 · 日本語 · Tiếng Việt · Bahasa Indonesia · 한국어 · Español · Português · Русский · Українська · Français · Deutsch · 繁體中文 · हिन्दी · Türkçe · Italiano · Polski · العربية · Català

A 0.10.2 development build with a scripted test model, in Full Access inside a throwaway workspace. The edit, three tests and a sub-agent review ran for real.

View the Codewhale × OrcaRouter offer. Codewhale earns a referral fee from OrcaRouter.

Install

macOS and Linux:

curl -fsSL https://codewhale.net/install.sh | sh

The installer puts checksum-verified codewhale and its short alias codew in ~/.local/bin. If your shell then says command not found, run the PATH line the installer prints (details). codewhale update upgrades it. These commands install the latest release. This page follows main, so a feature marked with a version arrives in that release; the changelog lists what each release adds.

Windows, npm, Cargo, and other ways to install 
winget install HunterBown.CodeWhale  # Windows x64 (or Scoop, or the installer from GitHub Releases)
npm install -g codewhale            # wraps the same release binaries
cargo install codewhale-cli --locked  # crates.io; can trail GitHub Releases

Prebuilt binaries cover Linux, macOS, and Windows on x64 and arm64. Nix, Homebrew on Linux, Android/Termux (preview), and manual downloads are in the installation guide, and containers in Docker. Stick to one install method per machine; otherwise two copies end up on PATH and whichever comes first wins.

Quickstart

  1. Commit or stash your work, then run codewhale from the root of a git repository. By default (Accept Edits) it edits files in the repository without asking and asks before each command; Shift+Tab steps the permission dial when you want it to ask more or less.
  2. Run /provider (or press F3), pick a provider, paste its API key, and choose a model. DeepSeek is the default provider. With no key, pick a local runtime instead. If no provider is configured and Ollama is already serving a chat model, Codewhale uses it automatically; from 0.10.2 it offers it when you send your first message.
  3. Type a task:
Fix the failing tests and explain what changed.

Read-only commands run straight away. For any other shell command Codewhale asks first: y runs it once, a allows commands like it for the rest of the conversation, n refuses. /undo takes back your last request and its file changes. /help lists commands and keys.

For scripts and CI, codewhale exec runs one task without the interface. By default, --auto uses Full Access: tools run without asking, shell commands have no Codewhale sandbox, and trust mode lets file tools write outside the workspace. Add --sandbox workspace-write to keep the shell sandbox and file-tool workspace restrictions, with trust mode off:

codewhale exec --auto --sandbox workspace-write "fix the failing tests and explain what changed"

Modes and permissions

A fresh install starts in Work mode with the Accept Edits permission. One dial switches both: Shift+Tab steps Ask → Accept Edits → Plan → Auto-Review → Full Access.

Switch with Options
Mode the Plan stop on Shift+Tab, or /mode Plan reads and searches but changes nothing. Work (every other stop) edits files and runs commands; start a goal with /goal when a request needs more than one turn.
Permission Shift+Tab Ask asks before every file edit and every shell command that is not read-only. Accept Edits applies file edits in your git repository without asking and still asks before commands. Auto-Review lets rules and a reviewer model approve routine calls and refuses high-risk ones; switch to Ask to approve those yourself. Full Access never asks, and commands can reach anything on this computer; repository rules and managed policy still apply.

See the modes and permissions guide for the details.

What it does

New in 0.10.2

  • /pet on turns your terminal into an animated whale that shows what the agent is doing, while the message box stays live. Its 980 particles spell the current step in English, Chinese or Japanese.
  • /workbar terminal shows the shells the agent is running as they run. Type into one, or press Ctrl+N for a shell of your own (macOS and Linux).
  • /undo takes back your whole last request in one step, including every file it changed, and /diff works in folders without Git.
  • When a plan is ready, Codewhale asks whether to start Work with Ask or Auto-Review, or keep planning.
  • /color gives each chat its own composer color, saved with the session.
  • web_search can use DeepSeek's new Search API: set [search] provider = "deepseek" with a DeepSeek key.
  • Outside Full Access, a curl or wget that would upload a credential never runs without your approval, and a command that hides invisible Unicode is refused. write no longer replaces a file the agent has not read, or one that changed after it read it.

Models

More than 40 providers are built in, including Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Google, Mistral, Moonshot, OpenRouter, and xAI. Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works, and so do local models through Ollama, vLLM, or SGLang. The default is DeepSeek's deepseek-flash, which DeepSeek moved to DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 on 2026-10-17; 0.10.1 runs it without an update (details).

/model switches models between turns, and /model auto picks one for each turn (/router sets up how). /turn inspect shows which model a turn used, what it cost and how long it took. codewhale auth chatgpt lets you use a ChatGPT plan instead of an API key (experimental). See Providers.

Receipts and undo

/receipts, or codewhale receipts --last after you quit, lists the files changed, commands run, web and MCP calls, agents started, approvals and who gave them, and failures. /undo takes back your last request and the files it changed, in one step and without trust mode. /restore rolls the whole workspace back to an earlier snapshot; because that overwrites later edits, it needs /trust on or Full Access. See Receipts.

Exec runs that offer tools are saved in every output format, so codewhale receipts --last works after exec --auto, including --json. Answer-only text and --json runs are saved only when resuming or when conversation compaction starts; use --output-format stream-json to always save them for receipts or exec --continue.

Longer work

/goal sets an objective that carries across turns. Codewhale can split work across sub-agents, run a fleet of agents, or follow a workflow checked into the repository.

Coming from another agent

Codewhale reads AGENTS.md on its own. Instruction files written for other tools, such as CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules, or .github/copilot-instructions.md, load only when you opt in with project_instruction_imports = ["claude"] (or "cursor", "cline", "windsurf", "copilot", "all") in your config; see config.example.toml. Codewhale warns when it finds one it did not load.

/import-claude prepares an import of your Claude Code settings and MCP servers for you to review. /plugin install accepts Claude Code plugins containing skills, commands, agent profiles, and MCP servers, and refuses plugins that need hooks or LSP servers (details).

Extensions

Connect MCP servers, add skills and plugins, and run hooks on session and tool events. Code mode (experimental, on by default) lets the model write one execute_tools program that calls several MCP and plugin tools; each call still meets your approval rules and keeps its receipt. The independently installed Computer Use plugin (experimental, macOS only) can observe and operate other apps. It stays off until you review its access and enable it (guide).

Ways to run it

Command What it does
codewhale The interactive terminal app
codewhale exec "…" One task without the interface. On its own it answers without using tools; --auto enables tools with Full Access by default, --sandbox workspace-write restricts them, and --output-format stream-json streams events as JSON
codewhale web A local web UI on 127.0.0.1 (guide)
codewhale review --pr N An advisory review of a GitHub pull request. The GitHub bot setup generates a pinned workflow for automatic reviews and @codewhale review, using your own model key and optional App identity
codewhale app-server --http The Runtime API, a local HTTP API for threads, events, approvals, and each turn's file changes
codewhale serve --acp The Agent Client Protocol over stdio, for editors such as Zed

The terminal app, exec, web, and the Runtime API share one engine (architecture). A community-maintained VS Code extension connects to it from the sidebar (source). A native desktop app built on the Runtime API is in development; it has no public download yet.

Cost and accounts

Codewhale is free and MIT licensed. With your own API key you pay the provider directly; local models need no key. The footer and /cost show what a session has cost when the price is known, and an unknown price is shown as unknown, never as free.

You don't need an account. Keys you add with /provider stay on your machine.

Safety and privacy

In Ask and Auto-Review, commands run in an OS sandbox where the system has one: Seatbelt on macOS, and bubblewrap on Linux when it is installed. Windows has no OS sandbox yet, and Full Access turns the sandbox off. Inside the sandbox, shell commands cannot read credential stores such as ~/.ssh, ~/.aws and .env files; from 0.10.2 the same rule covers terminal sessions and more file tools. /preview-request shows a redacted preview of the next request without sending it.

Telemetry is on by default. It sends aggregate counts (version and platform, session length and outcome, which built-in providers you used, feature and error counts) with a random install ID that rotates every 90 days, and never conversations, code, prompts, model names, file or repository names, or credentials. codewhale config set telemetry false turns it off. At startup Codewhale also checks GitHub for a new release; set CODEWHALE_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1 to skip that. More in authorization order, sandboxing, and telemetry.

Documentation

Start here Reference
Installation Configuration
Providers and local models Architecture
Modes and permissions Runtime API
Keybindings Plugin authoring
GitHub PR review All documentation

Community

Codewhale is what it is because of its community, and all feedback is welcome: a bug, an idea, or something that looked or felt wrong. Open an issue for any of these; an issue is also the best place to start a new feature. Pull requests are welcome for fixes, translations, providers and planned work. The contributing guide shows where each kind of help goes, and the roadmap shows where the project is headed. Contributors keep credit for the work that lands, and the repository layout shows where things live.

Chat on Discord, or add the maintainer, Hunter, on WeChat (hunterbown) and ask to join the Whale Brothers group. Everyone is welcome.

History and license

Codewhale started as deepseek-tui and still reads that project's configuration and sessions. It is independently maintained and not affiliated with DeepSeek or any other model provider. Thanks to everyone who has contributed.

MIT. Code adapted from other open-source projects is listed in the third-party notices.

releases.name: Codewhale v0.10.2
releases.body:
## What's in v0.10.2


Codewhale v0.10.2 adds an animated pet view (`/pet on`), a live Terminal work
dock, per-chat composer colors (`/color`) and a one-time note on the first
start after an update that says what changed. It closes three session
data-loss paths and a `codewhale web` session leak; adds the default Runtime
daemon socket locations to the sandbox deny-list; holds a `curl` or `wget` that uploads a
credential; refuses shell commands containing invisible Unicode; keeps the
Linux sandbox working when a hidden credential directory is a symlink; and
reduces idle TUI redraw work. `/undo` takes back a whole
request, including long and multiline prompts. `exec --auto` explains its
Full Access default, honors an explicitly stricter sandbox, and saves
tool-enabled runs and their failure receipts. Local runtimes appear during
onboarding, `/diff` works outside a Git repository, DeepSeek's Responses route
no longer rejects replayed tool history, and contributor fixes improve token
accounting, relay model lists, localized replies and Windows launcher
guidance. Delegated work continues without model-invented turn or time caps,
and independent workflow steps can continue after another

releases.name: v0.10.1
releases.body:
> **Codewhale** is the public product from Shannon Labs. The `codewhale`
> command, npm package, and release-asset names remain lowercase technical
> identifiers. The legacy npm package `deepseek-tui` is deprecated and
> receives no further releases. Users coming from v0.8.x legacy `deepseek` /
> `deepseek-tui` names should migrate with `docs/REBRAND.md`.

## Install

### Recommended — official GitHub release

New macOS/Linux install (checksummed binaries from this release):

```bash
curl -fsSL https://codewhale.net/install.sh | CODEWHALE_VERSION="v0.10.1" sh
"$HOME/.local/bin/codewhale" --version
```

For Windows, use the matching installer or archive below. For an existing
direct install, run `codewhale update`; it prints the executable path and
keeps newer builds. If the install directory is occupied by a different build,
use the fresh-directory migration in [the installation guide](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/CodeWhale/blob/main/docs/INSTALL.md).

### Secondary packaging — npm and Cargo

```bash
npm install -g codewhale
# or build from source
cargo install codewhale-cli --locked
```

The wrapper downloads the matched `codewhale` and `codew` command assets
from this Release.

aiSummary.oneLiner: An open-source terminal coding agent that runs directly in your command line to modify codebases autonomously.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: CodeWhale is an interactive terminal coding agent designed to run seamlessly in the command line interface without managing heavy IDE extensions. It allows users to query and chat with LLMs while giving them the ability to natively run bash commands, read local files, write and edit code, and access tools over the internet via DuckDuckGo. The agent leverages Claude-3.5-Sonnet to orchestrate actions in an iterative feedback loop where it can read its environment, make changes, verify the outcome, and apply recursive solutions. The interface is highly optimized for terminal environments utilizing python-prompt-toolkit.
keyFeatures: Terminal execution loop: Executes natively in the terminal without requiring heavy web interfaces or editor plugins.
Autonomous shell commands: Has the ability to automatically execute bash scripts and shell commands to explore its environment.
File reading and writing: Natively accesses local filesystem files to implement and refine code blocks.
Web search integration: Incorporates search functions utilizing the DuckDuckGo API to research solutions and verify bugs online.
Local memory and config: Persists AI interactions and configurations gracefully within local storage for continuity.

useCases.title: Headless Server Maintenance
useCases.description: Administrators use the terminal agent over SSH sessions to parse confusing log files and suggest command line fixes.

useCases.title: Rapid Test Generation
useCases.description: Developers use the agent to write test cases and verify execution results iteratively without breaking terminal focus.

useCases.title: Unfamiliar Code Exploration
useCases.description: Engineers drop the agent into an unfamiliar directory structure and ask it to explain file connections or find specific logic.

useCases.title: Automated Debugging Workflows
useCases.description: Programmers allow the agent to repeatedly run compiler commands and autonomously read stack traces until it finds the root cause.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Developers and system administrators who require a fast, headless terminal coding agent capable of autonomously interacting with local files and bash sessions. They can query LLMs and natively execute shell commands to modify their codebases. It is ideal for iterative feedback loops during development.
